observations.why: Framing onboarding as checklist completion appeals to keeping what works (conservation) and mastery of required steps (competence), but no value is named or plainly appealed to — the motive is structural, not voiced.

Replacement of an old system with a newer one could gesture toward openness-to-change, but the text frames it as a routine update — no novelty or stimulation is appealed to; the value signal is too thin to commit.
